obligation: G054 transfer test of the per-organ activation-aware gate
verdict: THE RULE'S STATED FORM IS REFUTED. A weaker form survives, and is labelled as post-hoc.

what_was_predicted_before_the_arms_ran.predictor: r99 of H as a fraction of input dim, per organ, from 6 sampled layers

the_refutation: At 4 bits the ordering holds: the predicted gainer (down_proj) is +0.0079 held-out top-1 and the predicted loser (up_proj) is -0.0029. At 3 bits it INVERTS -- the predicted loser gains +0.0137 against the predicted gainer's +0.0019. A rule that reverses at a bit width is not the rule as stated.
and_the_opposite_configuration_wins_here: On Qwen3-0.6B, writer-only beat all-MLP at 3 bits on both ppl and KL. On Falcon3-1B all-MLP is best at BOTH widths (4b top-1 0.9413 / KL 19.7; 3b 0.8729 / 93.5), beating every single-organ arm. The practical advice the rule gave for one body is wrong for the other.

the_weaker_form_that_survives.claim: the gate may be an ABSOLUTE threshold on r99 rather than a within-model ranking. Every organ measured below ~0.3 gains and the one measured at 0.605 loses:
the_weaker_form_that_survives.consistency: a threshold between 0.287 and 0.605 fits all four. Falcon's organs are BOTH concentrated by Qwen's standard, which is why both gain there and all-MLP wins.
the_weaker_form_that_survives.STATUS: POST-HOC. This threshold was fitted to four points AFTER seeing them; it is not what was predicted. It is a hypothesis for a third specimen, and the threshold must be declared in advance of that run or the test is worthless.
the_weaker_form_that_survives.the_honest_alternative: the r99 signal may simply be weak and the Falcon differences (-0.0029 to +0.0137) small enough to be run-to-run noise on one corpus. A third specimen decides between 'threshold' and 'no rule'.

instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.defect: one d x d Hessian allocated PER ORGAN rather than per input site
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.cost: 38.7 GiB; fixed by keying on (layer, input_dim)

instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.defect: the fix also dropped accumulation to float32, which was unnecessary
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.cost: no memory was needed; reverted to float64

instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.defect: GPTQ's Cholesky failed on Falcon's ill-conditioned Hessians at 1% damping -- at leading minor 2039 on the 2048-dim site and 8180 on the 8192-dim one, identically under float32 and float64, so not a precision problem
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.fix: escalating damping 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%, with a COUNTED fallback. A silent fallback to round-to-nearest would have made the treated arm identical to the control and the experiment would have reported 'no difference' from two identical arms.
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.counter_reads_zero: The escalation counter recorded ZERO Hessians needing extra damping on the run that succeeded -- yet the identical call crashed on the two runs before it, under both float32 and float64. So the factorisation sits right at the positive-definite boundary and succeeds or fails depending on accumulation order across LAPACK threads. The escalation makes it robust either way; the counter says it was not needed THIS time, not that it never is.
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.consequence_for_the_earlier_numbers: The 4-bit and 3-bit rtn/gainer/loser figures from the crashed run are BYTE-IDENTICAL to this one's (0.9286/0.9365/0.9257 and 0.8397/0.8416/0.8534). Only gptq_all was missing. The earlier distrust was over-cautious rather than wrong, and the conclusion is unchanged.

instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.defect: 18 float64 eigendecompositions of an 8192x8192 matrix for a shape statistic
instrument_defects_found_and_fixed_durin.cost: ~30 minutes single-threaded; now 6 sampled layers in float32, with the per-layer range reported so the sample is auditable

cost: 543.9s CPU per specimen end to end
